description: At **25**, **Orson Welles** directed *Citizen Kane* (**1941**). The film invented a new language: deep focus, flashbacks, and a hunt for one mysterious word, Rosebud.

hero.hook: A 25-year-old prodigy filmed a press tycoon and invented modern cinema.

blocks.text: For decades, critics have ranked *Citizen Kane* (**1941**) among the greatest films ever made. Its director, **Orson Welles**, was only **25**. The film tells the life of a press tycoon, Charles Foster Kane, and asks a simple question: can you ever really know a man?
Beyond the plot, Welles invented a new language. He mixed the techniques of silent film and sound film to talk about power, loneliness, and memory.

**George Orson Welles** made his name first in the theater, then on radio. On **October 30, 1938**, he adapted *The War of the Worlds*. By imitating a live news bulletin, he convinced listeners that aliens had landed. Part of America panicked. Overnight, Hollywood wanted him.

blocks.caption: 1938: Welles terrifies America with a fake radio report

blocks.text: [[RKO Pictures]], a big studio in trouble, offered Welles a rare contract: complete freedom of subject and [[Final Cut]], the right to decide the final edit on his own.
In Hollywood, a beginner almost never held that much power. Welles used it to control everything: script, casting, images, sound.

sections.title: The prodigy who got every right

blocks.text: With his cinematographer **Gregg Toland**, Welles refused the usual blurred backgrounds. They insisted on [[deep focus]]: everything stays sharp, from the front of the frame to the far wall. Several actions can play out at once in the same shot, with no cut.

blocks.caption: In Citizen Kane, every shot tells several things at once

blocks.text: Welles also filmed from low angles, the camera set near the floor, to enlarge his characters and stress their power. Ceilings became visible. The space speaks as much as the dialogue.

sections.title: Deep focus changes the way we look

blocks.text: The film starts with the ending: Kane dies alone in his palace, [[Xanadu]]. His last word is **“Rosebud.”** A reporter starts digging. Through flashbacks, friends and enemies tell contradictory versions of the same man.

Welles refused simple biography. To some, Kane is an idealist. To others, a tyrant. The viewer assembles the pieces without ever reaching a single truth. The mystery of Rosebud stays an elegant decoy, a key far too small to open a whole life.

[[William Randolph Hearst]], a real press tycoon, recognized himself in Kane. He tried to smother the film with a boycott in his newspapers and pressure on the theaters. *Citizen Kane* flopped on release. Later, the [[French New Wave]] made it a banner: the director-author who controls everything.

events.detail: The film opened and failed at the box office.
events.title: Citizen Kane

blocks.text: *Citizen Kane* proved that a film could be an investigation into power and memory. Its sharp images, its flashbacks, and its freedom in the editing room invented a modernity that cinema is still exploring.

sections.title: A cursed film, then a model
